contradictions.title: F2-PREP-005's Selected Pilot Boundary Charter (Sec.10) lists Notifications as an allowed inbound caller of Imaging ("overdue-lab-adjacent digest, currently a Low-risk violation to be formalized"); F2-PREP-006-C (SE-03) and F2-PREP-006-D (scope expansion 2) both independently re-read routes/notifications.ts in full plus grepped every prisma.* call site and found ZERO references to any Imaging-owned Prisma model anywhere in that file - only prisma.labWorkOrder.findMany (a Labs-owned model) at line 165.
contradictions.resolution: RESOLVED. F2-PREP-002's original IMG-09 edge (which the charter's Sec.10 traces back to) grouped Imaging together with Attachments/Inventory/Labs/Storage under one research-convenience cluster code also spelled "IMG" - a naming collision with F2-PREP-001/005's actual IMG domain code, not a real Imaging caller. Two independent, deeper, source-re-reading passes (006-C, 006-D) confirm notifications.ts's overdue-lab digest reads Labs' own labWorkOrder model, never an Imaging model. Notifications is REMOVED from the accepted-inbound-caller list. The charter's Sec.10 text is superseded by this consolidation on this specific point; F2-PREP-002's IMG-09 edge itself is not incorrect, only its cluster-label was ambiguous - no correction to F2-PREP-002's own file is made or required by this task.

contradictions.title: F2-PREP-006-A's file inventory names the JSON companion 'F2-PREP-006-B_imaging_data_storage_tenant_kvkk.json' in its own inspectedPaths list, while the actual merged filename on origin/main is 'F2-PREP-006-B_imaging_data_storage_kvkk.json' (no 'tenant' in the name); the task brief handed to this consolidation task also uses the 'tenant_kvkk' spelling.
contradictions.resolution: RESOLVED. Confirmed via git ls-tree against origin/main that the real, merged filename omits 'tenant'. This document and its JSON companion cite the real filename throughout. No sibling evidence file is modified to fix this cosmetic reference.

contradictions.title: F2-PREP-006-A's brgRoleClassification.selected records BRG's role as an 'unresolved combination (split by edge)' and explicitly defers the module-vs-submodule-vs-two-separate-modules question to this task; F2-PREP-006-B independently treats IMG+BRG as 'two sub-domains within the single modular-monolith Imaging boundary' without further split; F2-PREP-006-C's migration order (step 4) treats imagingBridgePublic.ts as already a complete, sufficient module boundary requiring only documentation, silently leaving BRG-RT-01..08's admin edge unaddressed.
contradictions.resolution: RESOLVED by this task's own decision (Sec. below): BRG remains ONE module (a named sub-module of the Imaging domain boundary, not a separate deployable, not merged into IMG), organized internally as two documented edges (device-facing adapter/ACL edge = imagingBridgePublic.ts; admin-facing domain-logic edge = BRG-RT-01..08, today physically inside imaging.ts). Physical relocation of the admin edge alongside the device edge is scheduled as additive Stage 5 work, not required before the contract itself is defined.

contradictions.title: F2-PREP-002's original F2-CC-14 candidate names only two write-side methods (markStorageMissing, redactForAnonymization). F2-PREP-006-C independently found and evidenced two additional cross-domain read-side direct-Prisma-access sites (DAV-01, DAV-02) and one direct-storage-access site (SB-01) that map onto the same Privacy callers but are not covered by F2-CC-14's original write-only scope.
contradictions.resolution: RESOLVED by revising F2-CC-14's scope (see f2cc14Decision.revisedScope for the unchanged original command methods markStorageMissing(imageId)/redactForAnonymization(imageId), which belong to the ImagingLifecyclePort facade and are not separately numbered entries in acceptedContractCatalogue.commands[]; see acceptedContractCatalogue.queries IMG-QRY-13/IMG-QRY-14 for the two new query methods added by this revision) to add query-side methods alongside the original two commands, rather than proposing a second, competing port. This is the 'accepted, revised' outcome for F2-CC-14 required by the task brief.

contradictions.title: F2-PREP-006-A's overlaps[] (OVL-01) and F2-PREP-006-C's headline finding #3/#6 both independently document the duplicated ingest transaction (manual vs bridge) and the ImagingRequest PATCH concurrency gap, but neither task states whether either is a 'blocker' in the same vocabulary the other uses ('risk' vs 'blocking prerequisite').
contradictions.resolution: RESOLVED by this task assigning each an explicit blocker classification (see blockerDecisions[]) using one consistent vocabulary across the whole contract.

duplicateIngestConvergenceDecision.detail: Introduce one shared internal application-service function (e.g. ingestImagingStudyCore()) called by both IMG-RT-09 (manual upload) and PUB-RT-02 (bridge ingest), carrying the common skeleton (file-signature validation already shared via imagingUploadValidation.ts -> storage save -> prisma.$transaction creating ImagingStudy+ImagingImage and conditionally advancing a linked ImagingRequest -> rollback-delete-file on failure -> audit log), while each route keeps its own distinct pre/post logic (manual: patient/appointment/case link resolution via validateClinicalLinks; bridge: ingestKey recomputation/dedup/P2002-race handling and agent-status touch). Also fixes OVL-02 (bootstrap's hardcoded update-policy stub) by having it call getBridgeUpdateConfig() like the dedicated update route.

imagingRequestPatchConcurrency.detail: Blocking before UpdateImagingRequest/CancelImagingRequest are exposed as commands any external caller (beyond imaging.ts itself) can invoke through the new facade. NOT blocking for Stage 0 (characterization tests may and should characterize the current unlocked-clobber behavior) or Stage 1 (additive facade with no new external caller yet).
imagingRequestPatchConcurrency.targetStageToResolveBy: Before Stage 3 (Privacy/KVKK caller migration) if request-mutation is ever included in that migration; must be resolved no later than Stage 2.

pzImg03.decision: REMAINS OPEN - not resolved by this task.
pzImg03.detail: F2-PREP-006-B refined its status from 'location unverified' to 'location resolved, authentication confirmed, RBAC granularity unproven'. Backup RBAC proof is INSUFFICIENT (single-tier authenticatePlatformAdmin only, no role/tier field on the platform-admin principal, no step-up authentication on the restore-capable endpoints specifically). Not a blocker for Stages 0-3. IS a blocker for the Backup/Storage migration stage (Stage 4) fully closing its KVKK-safeguard claim - the migration (formalizing fileBackupService as an accepted shared-infrastructure/adapter exception) may proceed on schedule, but this contract does not and cannot claim that migration closes any KVKK safeguard until PZ-IMG-03 is independently resolved by a separately-authorized security task.

finalReadinessDecision.rationale: Evidence across all four discovery packages (A/B/C/D) is deep, mutually corroborating, and resolves cleanly into one contract with only 5 contradictions, all Low/Medium severity and all resolved above. Imaging's structural profile remains the cleanest in the program (zero live cross-domain transaction coupling, DAV-06; only 2 real cross-domain violations, both metadata-only and already mapped to a named port). However, real, named blockers exist before Stage 1+ (CR-03/BLK-02 before request-mutation exposure; PZ-IMG-03 before any Backup/Storage KVKK-safeguard closure claim; a schema migration recommended before Stage 5 closes) - these do not block writing and running the characterization-test suite itself (Stage 0), which by design characterizes current behavior INCLUDING these known gaps. Runtime modularization (Stage 1 and beyond) is explicitly NOT approved by this decision.
notApprovedItems: Closure of PZ-IMG-03, R-070, R-046, or R-071
